The one-paragraph answer

DCAM (Data Management Capability Assessment Model) is the Enterprise Data Management Council's framework for measuring data management maturity. It is widely adopted in financial services and increasingly in other regulated sectors. In version 2.2 DCAM defines 38 capabilities and 136 sub capabilities across eight components, scored on a six level maturity scale that runs from Not Initiated to Enhanced. Version 3 was announced on June 30, 2025, and the EDM Council's 2026 benchmark report describes version 3.1 as current, with eight components, 34 capabilities and 101 sub capabilities. The framework is available only to EDM Council member firms.

The pain DCAM is solving for our readers

Financial services companies need to demonstrate data management maturity to regulators, buyers, and insurance underwriters. Anecdotal claims are not enough. DCAM provides a standardized benchmark: what capabilities exist, at what maturity level, with what evidence. Companies can measure themselves, plan improvements, and demonstrate progress. Regulators use DCAM as a de facto benchmark for financial-services data management.

What DCAM covers

The eight components, version 2.2

Data Management Strategy and Business Case, Data Management Program and Funding Model, Business and Data Architecture, Data and Technology Architecture, Data Quality Management, Data Governance, Data Control Environment, and Analytics Management.

What version 3 changed

Version 3 adds a Business Data Knowledge component, folds the two architecture components into one, widens the Data Control Environment to take in data management operations, and adds guidance for AI deployment and cloud data. It has eight components, 34 capabilities and 101 sub capabilities.

Maturity scale

Six levels, scored 1 to 6: Not Initiated, Conceptual, Developmental, Defined, Achieved and Enhanced, with defined characteristics at each level.

Assessment methodology

Standard questionnaires, evidence collection, and scoring for consistent benchmarking.

Why DCAM matters to you

The EDM Council says DCAM assessments give market authorities demonstrable and auditable evidence that a firm has adopted data management best practice. It also says the model maps directly to the risk data principles of BCBS 239, the Basel Committee's standard for risk data aggregation, and to privacy regulation such as GDPR. That is the practical reason it took hold in banking first: a firm under BCBS 239 can show its work in a form a supervisor can compare across institutions.

What the research says about DCAM

The academic literature on DCAM is ahead of most corporate practice, and it is unusually blunt. Two findings are worth putting in front of any executive who thinks this is a compliance formality.

“failure to do so can result in inaccurate analytics and unreliable decisions”

Gupta, Patel, Khan et al., ACM SIGKDD (2021)

That is the gap between having AI and governing it. The second finding is the one that tends to change the room.

“Effective data governance is important for minimizing data breach activity and mitigating bias”

Pahune, Rewatkar et al., Big Data and Cognitive Computing (2025)

Neither of these is a fringe position. Both come from peer-reviewed work, and both describe the condition most organisations are actually in when the question about DCAM arrives from the board, the buyer, or the regulator.

How to run a DCAM assessment: a 5-step path

DCAM is a capability model, not a regulation, so there is nothing to comply with. What a firm does is assess itself against the model, and the order below follows how the EDM Council describes that work.

  1. Confirm you have access. DCAM is available only to EDM Council member firms. Check whether your employer is already a member. If it is not, a firm can still be assessed by engaging one of the Council's Authorized Partners.
  2. Set the scope and the depth. Decide whether the assessment covers the whole enterprise or one region, operating unit or data domain. Then choose the depth: a high level assessment of 38 questions that takes 2 to 6 weeks, or a granular one of 136 questions that takes 6 to 12 weeks.
  3. Score each capability on evidence. Score every capability from 1, Not Initiated, to 6, Enhanced. DCAM judges three things: engagement, meaning the right people with the right authority are taking part, process, and evidence, meaning the artifacts needed to audit the capability. A score with no artifact behind it should not stand.
  4. Compare with the benchmark and set targets. Set a target level for each capability rather than one number for the firm, and list the gaps. The EDM Council publishes benchmark surveys built on DCAM, so you can see where peers in your industry score before choosing targets.
  5. Reassess on a schedule. Run the assessment again at a fixed interval and after any major change to the program. The Council's Data Excellence Program, which formally recognizes organizations, is built on periodic DCAM assessments.

Why regulated firms reach for DCAM specifically

Because assertion is not evidence. A bank telling an examiner that its data management is sound is making a claim. A bank presenting a DCAM assessment, scored against a published capability model by a defined methodology, is presenting a measurement. Examiners can compare it across institutions and across time. That comparability is exactly why the framework took hold in financial services and why it is spreading to insurance and other regulated sectors.

The maturity scale is the useful part

Six levels, from Not Initiated through to Enhanced. Most institutions discover on first assessment that they are lower than they assumed. The EDM Council's 2020 Global Data Management Benchmark shows where firms really sit: across 20 capabilities, finance industry averages ran from 2.99 to 3.89 and other industries from 2.46 to 3.26. That is the Developmental level, where engagement is under way and little is yet defined and verified. The 2026 edition of the same benchmark found the pattern holding: across nearly all components most organizations still sit in the Developmental or Defined ranges, and financial firms continue to outscore other sectors. That result is uncomfortable and useful: it converts a vague sense that data management needs work into a specific gap list with a defined target state. A DCAM assessment that returns a flattering score has usually been run too gently to be worth anything.

What DCAM means for AI readiness

Every AI ambition depends on the data control environment DCAM measures. A firm at level two cannot reliably answer where its training data came from, whether it is accurate, or who authorised its use, which means it cannot answer a regulator's questions about the model built on it. Data maturity is not a prerequisite that can be deferred until after the AI is deployed. It is the constraint that determines whether the AI can be defended at all.

Questions people ask about DCAM

What is the current version of DCAM?

DCAM v3, which the EDM Council announced on June 30, 2025. Version 3 adds guidance for AI deployment and cloud data, aligns more closely with privacy, security and regulatory requirements, and uses a leaner structure. It introduces a Business Data Knowledge component and folds the architecture capabilities into a single component. The Council says later modules on data culture and risk control are planned.

Material written before the middle of 2025, including much vendor documentation, describes version 2.2. Check which version an assessment, a tool or a training course refers to before comparing scores.

What are the DCAM requirements?

DCAM is not a law, and nothing in it is legally required. It is a capability model. In version 2.2 the EDM Council describes 38 data management capabilities and 136 sub capabilities across eight components, each with objectives, assessment questions, the artifacts that count as evidence, and criteria for scoring. Meeting DCAM means producing that evidence for each capability and reaching the score your organization has set as its target.

Which two types of architecture are components of DCAM?

In DCAM version 2, two of the eight components are architecture components: Business and Data Architecture, which is component 3, and Data and Technology Architecture, which is component 4. Version 3 consolidates the architecture capabilities into one component.

What are the eight components of DCAM?

In version 2.2 they are Data Management Strategy and Business Case, Data Management Program and Funding Model, Business and Data Architecture, Data and Technology Architecture, Data Quality Management, Data Governance, Data Control Environment, and Analytics Management. The first two are the foundation, the next four are execution, Data Control Environment is the collaboration component, and Analytics Management was added in version 2.2.

How is DCAM maturity scored?

Each capability is scored from 1 to 6: Not Initiated, Conceptual, Developmental, Defined, Achieved and Enhanced. At the low end the work is not performed or is only being planned. At Defined it is documented and approved. At Achieved it is adopted and enforced, and at Enhanced it is integrated into how the organization runs and is being improved. A score has to be supported by evidence, which is what makes two assessments comparable. The Council sets Achieved, a score of 5, as the minimum goal for a capability. Some vendor guides describe five levels and leave Achieved out; the Council's own 2026 report gives six.

How are DCAM measures created, and how long does an assessment take?

The measures come from the model itself. Every capability and sub capability carries its own assessment question and scoring criteria, so an assessment is a structured walk through them, by interview or by survey, with or without collecting the evidence artifacts. The EDM Council describes two depths: a high level assessment of 38 questions that takes 2 to 6 weeks, and a granular assessment of 136 questions that takes 6 to 12 weeks. It can be run for the whole enterprise or for one region, operating unit or data domain.

Is DCAM free, and can anyone use it?

No. The EDM Council states that the DCAM framework, its documents and its training are available exclusively to member firms. Check whether your employer is already a member before assuming it is out of reach, because membership is held by the firm and not by the individual. A firm that is not a member can still be assessed by engaging one of the Council's Authorized Partners. The Council's partner fee schedule has a separate category for assessments of non member firms.

Who maintains DCAM, and who is certified?

The EDM Council maintains it, developed with its member organizations. Its website now also uses the name EDM Association. Individuals earn a DCAM certification by completing the training and passing an exam. Members may assess themselves, and both members and non members may engage one of the Council's Authorized Partners, of which it lists nearly 50. Organizations can be formally recognized through the Council's Data Excellence Program, which is built on periodic DCAM assessments.

Does DCAM address data risk?

Partly, and more is coming. Data governance and the data control environment are scored components today, and the EDM Council says version 3 lays the groundwork for a future module on risk control. It also runs a Data Risk Forum for members.

Is DCAM only for financial services?

No. It was developed for financial services and is now used across regulated industries. In the EDM Council's 2020 benchmark survey more than 30 percent of responses came from outside finance, including manufacturing, software and services firms.

How does DCAM relate to DAMA DMBOK?

They are complementary. The DMBOK is a body of knowledge that describes the practice of data management across its knowledge areas. DCAM is a capability model built to assess how mature a firm's program is, with scoring and evidence.

Where does DCAM fit in the work of SRJ Consulting?

The AI Governance Framework Crosswalk™ maps DCAM capability components to AI governance artifacts, so a firm that has been assessed can reuse that evidence when it governs AI.

The authoritative texts and agency pages behind this summary. We keep this page current, but where a compliance decision turns on exact wording, read the source. Anything concerning DCAM that carries legal consequence should be confirmed against the enrolled text or the issuing body, not against a secondary summary, including this one.
